column1: # Module 10 — AI security taster. Format: Text<TAB>tags. Card law: anki/CARD-RULES.md
What is prompt injection, in one sentence? {{c1::Text the model reads as DATA gets obeyed as INSTRUCTIONS}} — everything in context is just tokens, no trust label.
What is direct vs indirect prompt injection? Direct = {{c1::typed by the user}}; indirect = {{c2::planted in content the agent reads}} — the dangerous one for agents: {{c3::indirect}}.
What are the five prompt-injection families? {{c1::Direct override}} · {{c2::role-play framing}} · {{c3::encoding tricks}} · {{c4::output-channel abuse}} · {{c5::indirect (planted content)}}.
What is Willison's lethal trifecta? {{c1::Private data}} + {{c2::untrusted content}} + {{c3::external comms}} — all three means one poisoned document can exfiltrate.
Why can't prompt hardening fix the lethal trifecta? {{c1::The model can't reliably distinguish injected instructions from data — the mixing IS the vulnerability}}.
In the OWASP LLM Top 10, what is LLM01? {{c1::Prompt injection}}.
In the OWASP LLM Top 10, what is LLM02? {{c1::Sensitive information disclosure}}.
In the OWASP LLM Top 10, what is LLM03? {{c1::Supply chain — models, packages, and the skills/agents you install}}.
In the OWASP LLM Top 10, what is LLM05? {{c1::Improper output handling — model output executed without review}}.
In the OWASP LLM Top 10, what is LLM06? {{c1::Excessive agency — capability beyond the task's contract}}.
In the OWASP LLM Top 10, what is LLM07? {{c1::System prompt leakage}} — assume CLAUDE.md and skills are extractable.
In the OWASP LLM Top 10, what is LLM09? {{c1::Misinformation — confident wrong output acted upon}}.
In the OWASP LLM Top 10, what is LLM10? {{c1::Unbounded consumption — runaway loops, quota/cost burn}}.
Which two LLM defences survive a smart attacker? {{c1::Capability narrowing}} · {{c2::human gates on irreversible acts}} — both architectural, not prompting.
Why are input/output filters only speed bumps? {{c1::Paraphrase and encoding defeat them — they judge strings, not intent}}.
What was your estate's own excessive-agency finding? {{c1::ClaudeBridgeWorker pushed the WHOLE repo every ~5 min though its contract was machines/context/}} (ledger 108).
What does bypassPermissions remove, and what becomes the dominant risk? {{c1::The last human gate between model output and the machine}} — making {{c2::LLM05/LLM06}} dominant.
Which connector is the classic untrusted-content leg? {{c1::Email — anyone who can email you can place text in a session's context}}.
What is the threat-model question set? {{c1::What could go wrong}} · {{c2::who could cause it}} · {{c3::what stops it today}} · {{c4::cheapest control that would actually help}}.
A control you'd never tolerate is what? {{c1::Not a control — it's a wish}} (the honesty column).
